text_fidelity_a:
King Koil Twin Air Mattress with Built-in Pump - Double High Elevated Raised Airbed for Guests with Comfortable Top Inflatable Bed with 1-Year Guarantee from The Manufacturer This mattress looked great out of the box. Now less than ten days later it's on its way to the garbage bin.

It looked good at first. The material seemed high-quality and the built-in pump worked great to inflate it, relatively quickly. I went online while the mattress was inflating and read all of the manufacturer's suggestions, including the one to inflate it and let it sit overnight before use to "stretch out", then add more air. I followed all the instructions carefully.

Just a few hours after fully inflating the mattress and without anyone using it or even sitting on it, I pressed on it with my hand and noticed it was already mushy and not nearly as firm as when first inflated, so I topped the air off again and let it sit overnight without using it. The next morning it was mushy again, but I figured maybe this was the "stretching" the manufacturer was talking about. That night I inflated the mattress to full firmness, made up the bed, and went to sleep. About three hours later I woke up with the hard floor under me and a tangle of deflated air mattress wrapped around me.

So clearly, the mattress was defective and had arrived with a leak. Well, that happens. It was really unfortunate because I had no other bed at the time to use, but I had gotten a cheerful email from the manufacturer here on Amazon right after I ordered, telling me if I had any problems to contact them and they would be sure to honor that warranty twhich hey make such a big deal of offering, and make things right.

I emailed them to let them know that right out of the box the mattress was leaking air badly. They replied with the same instructions I found online, saying it was probably "stretching out" and I just needed to top the air off. I replied that I had now spent two nights on the mattress, and the only way to use it was to set an alarm to wake up every two-and-a-half hours to reinflate it before it went completely flat. I asked them to please do as they said and work with me to make it right.

That more than a week and three emails ago. I have emailed them over and over (the only way to reach them.) The manufacturer simply stopped responding after the first email. They did not provide any customer support, no advice, nothing. They did nothing at all to honor the warranty they offer. I tried finding a patch kit on my own for this thing, but I can't even find the leak, it seems to be in the sealing of one of the seams. It's basically garbage at this point, because it's useless. The photo is of it sitting waiting to go out with the trash less than two weeks after being bought.

If you look at the one and two star reviews, many people have had the same issue. With this mattress, it seems like either you are one of the lucky ones and it works perfectly out of the box, or it just doesn't hold air at all and you are screwed, because the manufacturer is not going to keep their word and honor that reassuring-sounding warranty that they offer to entice people into buying their expensive air mattress.

So, if you need a bed and want to roll the dice, try your luck. I did, and I certainly regret believing the untrustworthy, dishonorable shysters who manufacture the King Koil.

$150 dollars, straight out into the trash.
text_fidelity_b: King Koil Twin Air Mattress with Built-in Pump - Double High Elevated Raised Airbed for Guests with Comfortable Top Inflatable Bed with 1-Year Guarantee from The Manufacturer

Timbuk2 Catapult Sling The description above is pretty weak. This bag comes in 2 different sizes, medium and large. The medium Catapult bag is similar in length and height to the Timbuk2 small messenger bag, but much slimmer and made from lighter weight fabric (comparable to typical backpacks vs the heavyweight fabric that Timbuk2 uses for most of its messenger bags). The large Catapult is similar in length and height to the medium Timbuk2 messenger bag, but again much slimmer and lighter weight. The large Catapult bag is significantly larger than the size medium; large enough to easily fit the medium bag inside.

Because of the slim profile and lighter fabric, you really don't want to carry a heavy load in the Catapult bag. If you want to carry a pile of schoolbooks, then get a regular Timbuk2 messenger bag. The Catapult bags can carry an ipad (or similar), a thin windbreaker jacket, a small water bottle, a box lunch, and a few small tools. Maybe not both a big lunch and a jacket in the medium bag.

As with the regular Timbuk2 messenger bags, the Catapult bags are designed to be carried high on your back with the strap pulled tight. The built-in pad at the end of the shoulder strap emphasizes this. These will not be comfortable if you carry them at your hip like a purse. If you do carry them high on your back with the strap pulled tight, they are very comfortable and stable while walking or bicycling or even jogging. The slim profile and (included detachable) stabilizer strap keeps the bag close to your back so it doesn't shift around. With the medium Catapult bag, you really don't need to use the stabilizer strap, but it is nice to have included just in case.

I really like that the Catapult bags have straps on the front for carrying a bicycle U-lock. However, I do not like that the bag's main cover is held down by only Velcro (when you don't have a U-lock). I would feel safer with the clasps used on the regular Timbuk2 messenger bags. I think the Catapult bags have enough interior pockets for the slim size of these bags; there is a large pocket in back for your ipad and a couple of smaller pockets in front for small items.
text_fidelity_b: Timbuk2 Catapult Sling

text_fidelity_a:
Augason Farms Freeze Dried Vegetable Variety Pack 4 gallon Kit & Augason Farms Lunch and Dinner Variety Pail Emergency Food Supply 4-Gallon Pail Where I live it is important to have back up food sources. Sometimes we get severe weather and that can mean an inability to go to the grocery store, no electricity, or sometimes snowed in for a while. I always try to have some different foods on hand that are easy to fix for such times as that, but one thing I have not had is vegetables for long term storage, should we have to go through an extended time of roughing it.

WHAT IS THIS COLLECTION LIKE?
WHAT SIZE BUCKET?
First of all, it comes in a four gallon sized bucket which is square. That means it will fit on the shelf more easily and be easier to stack. This baby was SEALED tight. It has a tab that you pull which starts a plastic strip coming off from around the entire rim of the bucket. The size is 13 1/2 inches high and 10 inches square.

HOW WAS THIS BUCKET TO OPEN?
I have to say that this bucket was VERY difficult to open. If you are older, or have a weak grip, this might be very difficult to open- especially in an emergency. Of course, being hungry might motivate you enough to push through, but honestly, I am pretty strong and this particular bucket was so hard to open I had to get pliers and then pull with all of my might many times to work it off of the bucket.

WHAT IS THE BUCKET LIKE INSIDE?
Inside the rim is a rubberized seal. I would assume that the way this was sealed that it would withstand reasonable water around it- perhaps not for a really long time, but enough to keep the contents dry for a bit should you need to be in the rain or have a flood in your storage area. There is a little crunched up bunch of powder inside which I am thinking was at one time a moisture control tab, but I can not say for sure.

There is a bit more space in the bucket so that you could keep other freeze dried pouches in here, or perhaps plastic dishes or other things you want to put in with it for saving space, such as vacuum sealed spices, or other mixes you might have accumulated or made. It is important that they are sealed, however as you don't want to have bugs get into the bucket over time from just loosely bagged foods. Also I would avoid grains in a bucket like this as they can still hatch bugs which will eat through vacuum sealed bags- ask me how I know..

WHAT IS IN THE BUCKET?
This is where I was a bit disappointed. The outside clearly lists what is in the bucket, but for the price, I expected to have a little better quality than this. There are metallic bags in this bucket most of which are vacuum sealed. Two of them are not, however. One of them is onions, but the other was not even labeled. It turned out to be potatoes, but there was not anything on the bag at all to indicate that it was potatoes. I would have thought that it would be labeled and vacuum sealed for the onions and potatoes. Perhaps there is a reason why they are not.

HOW PRACTICAL IS THIS KIT?
This kit has 109 servings in it. That is a lot, but the problem is that each package of vegetables is the entire contents of the bucket. For instance, it might have 15 servings of peas in one pouch, but let's say you do not want to have peas all of the time. Perhaps you have a quick emergency for a few days and then it is over. The problem is that once you open the bag of peas, the shelf life goes down quickly.

So, once you open a bag, you have to finish it in a reasonable amount of time and keep ti sealed in a jar perhaps for longer storage. It will NOT last 20 years as advertised however once opened.

HOW IS THIS KIT BEST USED?
This kit is best used as a 1 week supply for food. A few weeks at best. That means if you buy this kit, then you will have to plan on using what is inside all at once- at least each vegetable that you open. That means you should buy multiple packs if you want to have a long term storage that you can rely on over an extended period.

DRAWBACKS
I would have liked to see the pouches broken down in thirds or even halves. That way if you open one, you still have another for future use, up to 20 years. I also was not sure why the potatoes and onions were not vacuum sealed and why the potatoes are not labeled. They are a part of the kit, so they should have been labeled like the rest of the bags in the bucket.

QUALITY
The vegetables tasted good- they are freeze dried which means that you can eat them as a crunchy snack food without breaking your teeth as you would with dehydrated food. You can also cook with them, but honestly they were so good as snacks that is how we enjoyed them. It is important that you drink plenty of water when eating freeze dried foods, however. We would always have them right out of the bag at our house which is the best way to have the most nutrients.

I love that this has no added sugar or other ingredients like most "survival" food does. It is just vegetables and that fits our family perfectly as we do not eat sugar or highly processed foods.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Although the bucket is very difficult to get into (at least this one was), the food inside is well protected from weather and elements. The food is sealed in large bags of each type, so you need to use up what you open in a reasonable amount of time. Not all of the bags were vacuum sealed and one was not marked, so I give this four stars for that.

As for the purchase and having it handy, it is an excellent kit to have on hand, especially if you live in an area that is prone to severe weather. I would reiterate that it would be best to have a collection of these handy as this one will only feed a small family for a short period of time.

I will update with more information should I have anything else to report in the future.
text_fidelity_b: Augason Farms Freeze Dried Vegetable Variety Pack 4 gallon Kit & Augason Farms Lunch and Dinner Variety Pail Emergency Food Supply 4-Gallon Pail

ECOSUSI Vintage Canvas Sport Tote Gym Bag Overnight Shoulder Bag Weekend Travel Duffel Bag Khaki [[VIDEOID:aed816f7c2aaf0d164823759a497b104]] [[VIDEOID:52b4d8939c55600f821168592f0cdb4e]] I received this bag directly from the manufacturer at no cost for evaluation, and here are my thoughts.

This is a very spacious and sturdy weekend bag constructed of rugged canvas that is well complimented by dark brown crazy horse leather trim. It's 22.5" x 14" size make it acceptable as a carry on by most airlines, and it's roomy enough to fit enough for a long weekend or a trip of about five days. We own several bags just like this, and I can tell you from experience that the biggest problem with this bag isn't what it can fit, it's making sure you don't pack too much and go over the airline's weight limit.

This bag looks really great, and it's built to last. Every seam is double stitched, and attachments, handles, straps and zippers are leather reinforced, then both stitched and riveted for extra strength. The bottom of the bag has metal feet to protect the bag from scuffs, and the leather band that runs along the bottom edge protects it from scrapes and bumps when being manhandled by baggage handlers.

It's got nicely rounded handles that are comfortable to carry, and the attachment for the handles are leather reinforced and double riveted for strength. The buckles on the handle attachment straps adjust enough to secure a jacket or travel umbrella along the side of the bag too. In addition to the handles, the bag has a detachable shoulder strap that adjusts long enough to carry the bag over a shoulder or cross body. It doesn't have any padded piece for your shoulder, but the strap wide enough to bear weight without digging into your shoulder.

This is a top loading bag with a wide 22.5" top zipper which makes it easy to pack, and it has two zipper pulls which can be brought together in the center and locked with a TSA approved lock so you can protect the contents of your bag whether traveling or using it at the gym. The zipper is heavy duty and functions smoothly, giving you a nice wide opening to the bag's interior for packing and unpacking. The zipper is both stitched in place as well as reinforced with leather, and the leather zipper pulls are sewn as well as riveted for strength and durability.

Most of the bag's storage capacity is within the main compartment, but it also has a zippered vertical compartment on one side that's large enough to hold car keys and other small items, and a larger zippered compartment on the other side that's a perfect place to store your boarding passes, wallet, ID, and passport for quick access.

The inside of the bag is fully lined in a dark brown cotton material, and it's mostly open storage, with two open pouches for cell phone and other gadget on one wall, and two long zippered pockets with a long open pocket between them on the other wall. I encourage you to watch my video to see how much stuff this bag can actually hold. I think you'll find it more than spacious enough for short trips.

Canvas is a very durable material that holds up to the rigors of travel very well, so this bag should last a long time. It also sheds water pretty well, which helps keep contents dry between parking lot and terminal, but you can always scotchgard it as well if you want to give it some extra protection. Be sure to let the bag air out to dry completely if the inside gets wet. As I already mentioned, we have several bags just like this one and we absolutely love them. This bag is rugged, well made, and holds a heck of a lot.
text_fidelity_b: ECOSUSI Vintage Canvas Sport Tote Gym Bag Overnight Shoulder Bag Weekend Travel Duffel Bag Khaki

text_fidelity_a:
Arrow Precision Inferno Wildfire Crossbow Package (225-Pounds) I've been hunting with Mathews compound bows for 20 years and reached a point in my age that I wanted to switch to a crossbow. I wanted to find the best bow for the money to start out. I like compounds but I wanted to stay as basic and simple as I could with the crossbow for service and maintaining accuracy so I wanted a recurve.
Long story short the Excaliburs are nice but to rich for my blood so I took a chance on the Wildfire II based on the reviews. I'm glad that I did.
Pros:
Excellent fit and finsh work on the entire bow. Definitely quality construction on par with any of the big name crossbow makers.
It seems as fast and they say it is. Once sighted in it is consistently accurate. I think this bow is on par with the Excalibur baseline bows Like the Axiom or Ibex if not better as this bow has a one peice Aluminum rail versus a plastic rail. Weight is not bad at all and it feels well balanced for free hand shooting. Soft touch Camo is awesome and a nice balance of pattern and color.
Thumb Safety just like a rifle. Not up on the side of the string latch like a lot of other crossbows and quiet as a mouse. Not a loud CLICK! when you take the safety off. The trigger does have some creep but is pretty smooth overall. The more I shoot the better it gets.
Shot noise is average and less than a pellet gun for comparison. It comes with factory installed limb dampeners that attach to the riser/limb. I also installed the SIMS LIMBSAVER kit and it definitely helped reduce the sound when fired.
Scope is actually very good quality and clarity. Super clean reticle and the adjustable illumination is great for early morning/late evening shots! I was thinking to buy a Nikon but this scope is really nice so I will keep using it.
Rope cocker, Arrows, quiver, and sling are very nice quality as well. Super sling swivels too!
Must haves:
Plano Soft bow case. Best priced case that actually fits the bow another really good option is the OMP Crossbow soft case. A little more in cost but has additional pockets for arrows etc.
Tenpoint ACUrope cocker (BEST). Compact and retractable. Works like a dream and has a belt pouch.
Carbon Express Bolts. Either the Piledrivers or if you want the best get the Maxima Hunters. Buy their lighted nocks for your hunting arrows.
Go ahead and buy the MTM bolt case for your extra bolts.
Scorpion Venom string wax. The bow comes with string wax but I feel the Scorpion is easier to use and stays super slick in all weather.
Rail lube. DO NOT USE STRING WAX! I did and it slowed down the bow and killed my accuracy. I had to clean the rail with rubbing alcohol and start over. Buy Excalibur rail lube and/or do some research on the bow forums on what the veteran shooters are using. Some recommend silicone spray and other types of lube. If you're going to hunt use something that doesn't have any odor. I ended up using Ultralube 4x. It's all natural and no odor.
NAP 100 grain Sptifire Edge mechanical broadheads. These are my personal favorite and for overall accuracy I prefer mechanicals over fixed blades for better flight at high speeds.
Target for field point is the Hurricane H25 hands down best practice target for the money. It stops the bolts no matter what and is heavy and stable. You don't need a stand for it.
Target for broadheads I recommend the Blobtarget or American white tale HybriMAT AP . They are both pricey (BT 18"x18"x10" $90 shppied) (HybriMAT AP 18"x18"x12" $129.95 shipped) but they will last you for years and years vs the cheaper ones that last a year and are still very expensive!
Update:
Bought a Prochrono on Amazon to check the speed of the bow and right now it is 315fps with the stock arrows and with the Maxima Hunters. Dyna Flight string should bring it up to as much as 330fps.
I ended up removing the limbsavers since they slowed it down (10fps!) and actually created vibration in the bow after the shot. To be honest the noise level is not much different without them.
Another update. Bow is shooting 330fps using Carbon Express 20" hunter maximas and 100gr tips. I switched to Black Eagle Spynal Tapp arrows and the speed is still on.
Final deer season tally is 3 does and i buck
text_fidelity_b: Arrow Precision Inferno Wildfire Crossbow Package (225-Pounds)

Stansport Aluminum Tent Peg, 9-Inch These stakes are well-constructed and can be pounded into reasonably hard soil without damage. I haven't destroyed any yet, but I do try to be careful when I'm pounding them into rocky ground. (A small, 8-ounce hammer works well. Larger hammers increase the likelihood of bending or breaking your stakes). The round cross section doesn't have the holding power of some of the flatter stake designs, so they don't hold as well in wind, in my experience. They're longer than most other after-market tent stakes, though (9 inches vs the more common 7-inches), which helps compensate. I like to have a few of these in my stake bag for places that the y-shaped stakes can't penetrate.

Some users have complained that they can't get their tent guylines through the holes in the silver heads. That isn't how they are intended to be used. Wrap your guyline or your anchor loop around the shaft of the stake, just below the silver head, and angle your stake to point it toward a point several feet below the center of your tent. These are fine stakes. Would like to try some of this style in a longer, 12-inch version, for larger tents that catch more wind and require stronger anchors.

L NOW Adjustable Mini Stair Stepper Exercise Equipment Step Machine [[VIDEOID:83c958ef59934ea5cf190154e38a240d]] I've had a compact stepper for a couple of years now. It's the perfect solution for my lifestyle. I don't have a lot of room for an exercise bike or elliptical but I still needed something that helped me get my exercise. I use the compact stepper while watching TV. It's quiet enough, but does have a slight squeak.

When I saw the L NOW Adjustable Mini Stair Stepper, I thought the design looked promising and it looked more compact. I gotta say, it works well, and so far, it's been pretty quiet. It has a step counter built in but no resistance adjustment. Still, the resistance for my 145lb frame is comparable to my original stepper set at about medium to high resistance, which is my normal setting anyway. The L Now is more compact and lighter, making it even easier to store away when I don't need it. After a 20 minute session, I work up quite a sweat.

Overall, I'm happy with my purchase and I've taken a couple of pictures and videos to compare the two machines side-by-side to help you make your own decision. I think my original stepper sold pretty well and I expect the L Now stepper to do well also.

text_fidelity_a: ABUS 4804 Steel-O-Chain Steel Bike Chain Lock Great lock for securing secondary components like seat and front wheel on your bike.  I live in Baltimore where bike theft is an issue, but not as bad as it is in bigger cities.  The general recommendations are U-Lock your frame and rear wheel first, then secure the front wheel and seat with something like a cable or chain lock.  I needed this longer length chain to secure my seat, and I use the shorter Abus steel chain lock to secure my front wheel to the frame.  This may be a little bit of overkill, but it is not unusual in Baltimore to see locked up bikes with the front wheel missing, and I overheard a woman in my LBS who was coming in to buy a new seat because hers had just been stolen.  These things can/do happen, and the harder you make it for thieves, the more likely the thieves are to pass you by for an easier target.  Seats and quick-release wheels are easy to steal when left unsecured, and they are expensive to replace.  A cable lock costs about as much, but is significantly easier to defeat than these chain locks.  I like these Abus locks (this one and the shorter one) because they are a small investment for a lot of peace of mind.
text_fidelity_b: ABUS 4804 Steel-O-Chain Steel Bike Chain Lock

Gelindo Tactical Backpack with Bladder - Insulated Military Pack with Molle System I bought this for my fiancé for Christmas, he needed a new emergency backpack. You never really know what you’re getting when you’re ordering stuff like this online...one review will say it’s garbage, the next will say it’s the best thing ever. I’m pretty good at judging which ones are accurate, and which ones are super-biased - either for or against.

This is a very good backpack! It’s worth more than what they’re charging for it. I looked (in person) at some 3.11 Tactical backpacks, and, this measures up in every single aspect, at a fraction of the price (for those that haven’t seen them, they’re generally well over $100). Also, the 3.11s that I looked at didn’t have padded waist straps like this one, and didn’t come with the bladder, like this one does. The padded waist straps alone up the value, plus there’s small zipper pockets on them to stash keys or whatever in...they don’t hold a plus size iPhone though. Just a smidge too small. You don’t realize how important padded waist straps can be until you’re stuck with carrying 30lbs on your back and those plain straps are digging into you, even through a heavier coat.

The padding in the back is just as good as the Swiss Army backpack I have, it’s not itchy if it gets against your skin, and it does pretty good at keeping you cool...as cool as you can be with a bag strapped to your back, at least.

There’s plenty of pockets so you can organize you’re supplies for better accessibility and it does have the nice straps on the bottom to attach a bedroll (yoga mat, if you choose) or pup tent. There’s plenty of places to add/attach other accessories and pouches. Also, the compartment for the bladder is insulated. I can’t really say how well because we haven’t tested it, but it seems it would be decent.

All around, this is just a really, really good pack, especially for the price! I fully intend on buying myself one very soon because all of my backpacks are shot (my “everyday”, and my emergency bags), and this just fit the bill...I almost kept it for myself! 😁
text_fidelity_b: Gelindo Tactical Backpack with Bladder - Insulated Military Pack with Molle System

NCAA Missouri Tigers Can Cooler, 16 I am a Pittsburgh Steelers fan, so I admit that I just picked this cooler for the colors, and I don't even know the Missouri Tigers. But cooler is incredibly well-made and I'm thrilled that I got it!

The first great surprise when it arrived was that it is made by Coleman, with tags on it to prove it. Coleman doesn't make bad stuff, in fact, they have a long history of well-made products, so that was a really nice bonus.

On top of that, there are all kinds of extras built into it. For example, when you lift the lid, there is a mesh ice-pack holder built right into the top of it. On the outside of it, there are mesh holders on each side (I use them for napkins, straws, or nutrition bars). Then in the front there is a nice zippered compartment that you can put things in. The zippers are high quality and the materials, inside and out, are high quality as well. The strap is strong and adjustable. Another nice perk is that it has a little pad where the strap will go over the shoulder, which really makes carrying it much more comfortable. The cooler holds a lot, and really does a great job at keeping things nice and cold. I just put my ice packs in it with our bottles, sandwiches, etc., and we are good to go.

I also got one of these coolers for a friend who is disabled and likes to keep a cooler next to her bed. Well, she'd gotten fed up with coolers that didn't keep things cold for very long and she had switched to using a spaghetti pot (for real!) with ice packs in it, to keep her ginger ale chilled, for constant nausea. She said that with a few frozen ice packs in it, she actually can go two whole days without having to replace the ice packs. She also said it fits great on her scooter when she's on the go.

I could have picked any of the NCAA teams that they make this cooler for, but I happened to pick the colors of my favorite pro football team, the Pittsburgh Steelers. (OK, I'm frugal and couldn't spring for the much more expensive Steelers cooler, but this way I get my team colors AND an awesome cooler.)
text_fidelity_b: NCAA Missouri Tigers Can Cooler, 16

Swagtron High Speed Electric Scooter with 8.5” Cushioned Tires, Cruise Control and 1-Step Portable Folding I bought for my wife and at first it was great but in less than four months it no longer was functional.

The unit fell apart primary due to the fact they are too cheap to use Loctite or equivalent to secure screws--only the brake unit had Loctite.

- month one the handle bar screws needed to be tightened every week
- month two the knob on the rear wheel cover which the neck lock to carry fell off
- month two the neck screw had to be tightened weekly
- month three brake needed to be adjusted--not a big deal, but..
- month four the neck screw' nut fell off and I could not find a replacement at Homedepot

Customer service was slow and they insisted I shipped the entire unit for warranty service. Why would I be expected to ship the entire unit back to have screws or other small parts easily replaceable by the customer?

I tossed the scooter in a corner in the garage so I can responsibly dispose of the battery, later, before tossing it in the trash.

Do yourself a favor and look at Xootr. Quality scooters that will last for ten years or more. They provide parts. It is NOT electric, however.

Spend you money elsewhere for these guys do not stand behind their product and have horrible customer service. I feel ripped off! Can you tell?

text_fidelity_a:
BubbaCapri Tumbler, 32 oz, Paradise Purple with Chevron I have a couple of other Bubba bottles, and more 32-oz water bottles than I can count (mostly Nalgene, a few others). I usually drink two 32-oz bottles of something every day -- usually water and/or a favorite Crystal Light mix. So I was interested to try out this Bubba tumbler.

I like the design -- a basic tumbler shape, silicone sleeve, flexible rubber-ish straw, tight-fitting lid. It's not spill-proof: the straw is inserted into a hole in the middle of the lid that has a small "divot" to allow air into the sealed tumbler so that you can sip. The straw fits nicely into the hole, but the divot leaves an opening for liquid to escape. Since I'm not very hard on my water bottles, I don't consider this a problem. I'm not prone to dropping or tipping them, so there shouldn't be a problem with spillage.

The sleeve provides *some* insulation so that my drink does stay colder longer than a non-insulated bottle, but not as long as a vacuum bottle. I hand-wash mine -- it's just something I do each night before I go to bed -- so I don't need to deal with removing and replacing the sleeve.

For the price, I think it's a good deal. I'm planning to purchase another one or two to have spares, and I'm definitely taking one of them along on my upcoming travels.
text_fidelity_b: BubbaCapri Tumbler, 32 oz, Paradise Purple with Chevron

ProsourceFit Yoga Mats 3/16” (5mm) Thick for Comfort & Stability with Exclusive Printed Designs I must admit that I have a bit of an obsession with yoga mats. Although I have an absolute favorite mat that I use regularly (a [[ASIN:B00IOT7Y1C Manduka eKO Lite Mat]] in green, my favorite color), and several others that I use for different purposes, I can't seem to resist trying new ones. I was particularly interested in this mat because I have never tried a mat from the ProSource brand.

This mat arrived rolled in a large box. Upon opening it, I found the mandala design very appealing, although I was less enamored with the pink color--I DO like pink, but unfortunately, this is somewhat of a Pepto Bismal shade. I also detected a scent that I've found to be common to new yoga mats, especially those made of more eco-friendly materials; to me, the fragrance is reminiscent of a plastic toy for a swimming pool. This scent was NOT as strong as some other new mats I have received, and it dissipated significantly when I left the mat lying out unrolled for several days. (For other mats, I have had to leave the mat lying out in the sun to get rid of the smell.)

The ProSource mat is 5mm, thicker than many average mats that are only 3mm. However, I found it to still feel quite lightweight. (I believe that it is lighter than my Manduka eKo Lite, which is only 3mm but very dense and high quality.) I was also extremely impressed with the stickiness of this mat. Virtually EVERY yoga mat that I have every tried (with the exception of my eKo Lite) has produced some sliding, particularly when my hands are on the mat for downward facing dog, but this mat kept both my hands and feet in place.

So far, I am quite happy with the performance of this mat. For the appearance, I would knock my rating down to 4 1/2 stars (I think I would have preferred the "Mandala" option, which has the mandala design but in a much more attractive teal blue color), but I would definitely recommend his ProSource yoga mat.
text_fidelity_b: ProsourceFit Yoga Mats 3/16” (5mm) Thick for Comfort & Stability with Exclusive Printed Designs

Speedo X-Flex Swim Goggle With all the chemicals used to keep swimming pools in good working order and as germ-free as possible, a good pair of goggles is indispensable if you're going to the pool to actually get wet. If you only venture poolside to lie on the deckchairs and soak up the sun, you need to stop reading this, and go look up "sunscreen", "sunshades" and "rum cocktails with little umbrellas."

However, once the top of your head is going below the surface of the water, you might want to invest in a pair of good quality goggles, and Speedo is the most trusted brand name in the swimming world. This pair is comfortable and fits securely through suction. It has a special headstrap system that makes adjustments in seconds, and the lenses are anti-fog with UV protection. As a former competitive swimmer, I can attest that these goggles are functional, and not just another pretty design.

I don't know if Jimmy Cliff ever used goggles, but I'm thinking that his version of the song "I Can See Clearly Now" is extremely applicable to this product.

I can see all obstacles in my way
Gone are the red eyes that made me cry
It's gonna be a bright (bright) bright (bright) sun-shiny day

Oh yes, I can take it now the pain is gone
Now that the eye-burning has disappeared
These are the goggles I've been waiting for
It's gonna be a bright (bright) bright (bright) sun-shiny day

text_fidelity_a:
Planet Bike Superflash USB bike tail light If you need a taillight bright enough in solid mode for foggy/rainy daytime riding, this is probably not the taillight for you.

I used the old AAA powered Superflash for many years and it was good enough for my type of riding. Mostly unlit trails. Some city riding. I always used the flash mode which is very attention grabbing. Rain, fog, snow, whatever. Solid mode is still good on a clear night, but not for low visibility daytime conditions.

The old Superflash had a tendency to pop off when riding over bumps. Also had a flimsy switch.

This model has built-in batteries which means it's one solid unit that wont fall apart. The switch is improved as well. I don't think it's really any brighter than the old one.

Cosmetically it is improved from the old model due to the black plastic housing. White plastic looks grungy after a while.

I still consider the Superflash to be a good value for the money.

Schwinn Insight LED Lighted ERT Youth/Adult Bike Helmet, Fits Head Circumferences 54-62 cm, Find Your Sizing, Multiple Colors My head is large, but not XL. I wear hat size 7.5, which is 60cm in circumference. This helmet is slightly too small for me. The sides are snug with the adjustment band loosened all the way. More importantly, the height is shallower than other bicycle helmets and more of my head is exposed even when the top of my head is firmly pressed against the inside of the helmet.

Weight of this helmet is 11 ounces, compared to 8 ounces for another helmet that I own. The extra weight is noticeable on my head. I presume that most of that weight is for the lighting system.

Most other lighted helmets that Amazon sells have a simple light that clips on to the back of the helmet. This helmet is much fancier with an array of lights and all the wiring built into the helmet itself. The lights cover a wide are of the front and back of the helmet and appear brighter than with other helmets. There are a few different lighting modes with the very obnoxious mode hopefully giving you a better change of attracting the attention of distracted drivers. Unfortunately, the manufacturer does not say how long the battery lasts. I will try to add that information after I do more testing.

For the price, this helmet is pretty nice. I just wish the large was larger.
text_fidelity_b: Schwinn Insight LED Lighted ERT Youth/Adult Bike Helmet, Fits Head Circumferences 54-62 cm, Find Your Sizing, Multiple Colors

text_fidelity_a:
Gonex Ultralight Handy Travel Backpack Packable Daypack 20L This pack is small enough to attach to a belt loop or store in a glove compartment. Even after my clumsy job of repacking it into the self-contained and integrated case it measured about 6x6x3 inches and is feather light.

Note that while the product photos (at the time of this review) look as though you are getting a backpack and a smaller case, you are only getting a single item. The smaller case shown is integrated into this pack and functions as the storage when not in use. Since the product description and other reviews have exhaustively covered the physical characteristics I will highlight my experience.

First, there are no real instructions, and when you first figure out how to unpack it you marvel at the full size. Then panic sets in because you cannot believe that you can repack it. Actually, both procedures are fairly intuitive. I had mine unfurled in mere minutes, and when it came time to repack I stretched the entire pack out, folded it over laterally, then continued folding it lengthwise until it fit into the zippered pouch that is part of the pack. Even I was able to accomplish that on the first attempt, and when you've done it a few times it literally takes less than a minute.

Second, it's surprisingly comfortable with the shoulder straps and fit. As others have mentioned it's not for heavy loads (although you can easily manage about twelve pounds without damaging or straining it. The zippers are decent quality and the compartment holds more than I would have guessed. I was about to cram a beach towel, a small bluetooth speaker and a water bottle in the pack with room for other odds and ends.

Overall, this is a great pack for those times when you wish you had one (like at a swap meet or farmer's market), and a grab-and-go for active folks. Even though the design implies occasional use, it can be an everyday pack as long as your loads are relatively light.
text_fidelity_b: Gonex Ultralight Handy Travel Backpack Packable Daypack 20L

text_fidelity_a:
FitDesk Desk Bike 3.0 - Folding Exercise Bike for Work from Home Fitness, Stationary Bike and Desk Exercise Equipment with Built-in Tablet Holder, Bike Desk Workout Equipment, Fully Adjustable & Lightweight Update 10/14/17
So yesterday I was riding my FitDesk when at about 8 minutes, I started to hear a soft clunking. It continued till I was finished. Today when I started pedaling, there was no noise, but after a few minutes the clunking started again, and it not only got a little louder, but I could feel the rubbing and clunking with each rotation; I found it distracting enough that I stopped earlier than I had planned. The pedals are nice and tight, and I haven't used this bike that much.

Update 04/19/17
The seat never felt that comfy, so I got the widest bike seat I could find - it's 13" wide, and that seems to work much better than the narrower seats, as my "sit bones" are over 10" apart.

Update 10/05/16
My husband cut down the saddle tube (part 66 in the manual) the seat sits on, cut two holes in the side for the pin to go through, and voila! The Fitdesk now fits me perfectly - and while I was concerned that sitting lower would make the desktop too high to use, it's actually more comfortable for me :) Next step will be to create a seat back that reclines!

Original review
There are a few things that stood out for me about the Fitdesk v2.0. First is the size of the cranks, 135mm, which is 35 to 40mm shorter than the cranks on most exercise bikes. Since I have short legs, the shorter (but not short) cranks were what first drew me to try the Fitdesk. I like the idea of being able to work while pedaling, but the second thing that stood out for me is Fitdesk's customer support. I emailed them tons of questions before buying; they answered every one quickly, politely and knowledgeably. They also read the questions on this listing, as I asked one and when no users responded, Fitdesk support did. I also like the configurableness (if that's even a word). If you want, you can get an adapter and use any bicycle seat on the Fitdesk; you can also get extenders to widen the desk section.

So I bought the Fitdesk, and pedaling is smooth and very quiet - quieter, actually, than my husband's Schwinn 170, which is a nice bike. It took my husband about 35 minutes to build my Fitdesk v2.0 (thanks, honey!), and when some missing parts were discovered, Fitdesk sent them to me and I had them in my hands in 4 days.

So why isn't this a 5 star review? First, this claim from the Fitdesk website - "Adjustable Lean. For a further "back lean" ride or a "forward lean" ride." Um, no. My Fitdesk's seat's furthest back lean is pretty much upright with just a hint of back lean; the other adjustments let you sit so your back is actually forward, which doesn't seem very useful to me. I would LOVE it if the seat had a couple adjustments allowing me to lean back further, and in fact that was one of the reasons I decided on the bike. Too bad it's not an accurate claim. I'd be one happy camper if I could adjust the seat back from upright to leaning back to leaning way back. Also the actual seat could be more comfortable, but everyone is different when it comes to seats. For now, it's more comfortable for me than most seats but after 30 minutes or so it gets just a little uncomfortable.

As a side note, my husband is a manufacturing engineer and CNC programmer, and he's considering whether he can make me a seat back holder that gives me the angles I want/need with the machines we have access to. In the meantime, the furthest back angle is good if you want to type.

Overall I like the Fitdesk quite a bit. The smooth, quiet action is very nice, the vulnerable parts of the body came wrapped so there's not a chip or scratch anywhere and Fitdesk support is really great. The desk itself is nicer in person than in pictures, and the rubber surface is just grippy enough; the desk fits my husband's 17" laptop well and my tablet very well. The computer's scan has a nice speed and seems very consistent. If only the seat back could be adjusted so it could either be used as it is now or lean back further, this would be a 5 star bike for me. As it is, the Fitdesk v2.0 is a very nice exercise bike and I'm really enjoying it.
text_fidelity_b: FitDesk Desk Bike 3.0 - Folding Exercise Bike for Work from Home Fitness, Stationary Bike and Desk Exercise Equipment with Built-in Tablet Holder, Bike Desk Workout Equipment, Fully Adjustable & Lightweight

RockyMounts Hooligan Chain Bicycle Lock First of all, this company really should say right in the product name that this is a BIKE LOCK. Nowhere in the listing at all does it say BIKE LOCK.

This bike lock and chain will definitely get the job done. The best thing about this set is that it comes with three keys. Of course you would expect to get two keys, but the third one allows you to keep on safely hidden at home or at work. If three people are sharing the bike then the third key is almost a must have. The lock mechanism is solid and it has a very soft barrier around it so if it happens to fall and hit your bike it will not dent and scratch easily. The chain is also covered in nylon to keep the chain from damaging your bike too. This one is listed as a level 6 security. The chain inside the nylon feels thick, but it is only a single link. The other thing that I don't love is the big 'amazon commercial' yellow sticker on the front that sticks out like a sore thumb. Of course, they need to market their product, but they could have added branding in a more subtle way.

bago Lightweight Small Hiking Backpack for Women and Men - 25L Travel Day Pack - Foldable Hiking Daypack Ultralight My husband was looking for a day pack. I bought him 6 backpacks to compare. The [[ASIN:B010LAU5CG Hiking Cycling Backpack, Sunhiker Sports Outdoor Backpack Bag Running Camping Backpack Water Resistant Lightweight SMALL Daypack 25L M441 (Black)]], the [[ASIN:B00DNTR5CQ Osprey Packs Momentum 22 Daypack (Spring 2016 Model), Carbide Grey]], the [[ASIN:B014EMLHDI Outlander Packable Handy Lightweight Travel Hiking Backpack Daypack, Grey]], the [[ASIN:B00FUWSTI8 Lightweight Rucksack 25L for men women kids - Foldable into Inner pocket (BLACK)]], the [[ASIN:B013K7CJD0 Cycling Hiking Backpack Sunhiker Water Resistant Travel Backpack Lightweight SMALL Daypack M0714 (Dark Green)]], and the [[ASIN:B01EH0YGSU Free Knight 25L Packable Handy Lightweight Travel Backpack Daypack-Lifetime Warranty (New Grey)]]. There were pros and cons for each pack. He decided to keep the [[ASIN:B010LAU5CG Hiking Cycling Backpack, Sunhiker Sports Outdoor Backpack Bag Running Camping Backpack Water Resistant Lightweight SMALL Daypack 25L M441 (Black)]]because it met his needs the best. We ordered all packs in gray, green, or black. We returned the other 5 packs. I liked 2 of the lightweight foldable packs - the [[ASIN:B014EMLHDI Outlander Packable Handy Lightweight Travel Hiking Backpack Daypack, Grey]]and the [[ASIN:B01EH0YGSU Free Knight 25L Packable Handy Lightweight Travel Backpack Daypack-Lifetime Warranty (New Grey)]]. I decided to order those for myself in Pink and Purple.
All of the packs had a mesh pocket on each side of the pack for water bottles. We tested them all with a Nalgene bottle and a bottle of water. All of the packs could easily hold the bottle of water. Some were a very tight fit for the Nalgene bottles. All packs had a main compartment with one or two pockets in the front of the pack. The main compartments varied from 561 cubic inches to 1386 cubic inches. 3 of the packs were lightweight, foldable, and storable in their own pocket.
Here are my summaries of this pack:
1071 cubic inches
17” x 10.5” x 6”
6 1/2” mesh pockets
Covers about 5 1/2” of bottles
Straps 3” wide
Hard to adjust shoulder straps, especially to loosen them
Straps feel soft and pliable
This pack has 3 main compartments. In the back is the largest zippered compartment. In the middle is a small zippered pocket. In the front is a mesh compartment which is held closed by a strap and buckle. I did not like having a mesh compartment.
Pros:
- Lightweight
- Handle at top of pack for an additional way of carrying it
- Side pockets fit a Nalgene bottle
- Medium sized zippered pouch inside the large compartment – this is where the pack is stored when folded
- Large pocket inside on the back of the large compartment
- 1 extra loop on outside bottom of pack.
- Extra side support straps
Cons:
- No back padding and did not keep it’s shape. Typical for a foldable pack.
- Some padding on the back panel
- Shoulder straps were several layers of mesh but NOT fortified with the nylon fabric
- Things stored in front mesh compartment would get dirtier and wetter than in a pack with a zippered fabric covered compartment.

I returned this pack. It was a nice foldable pack, but I didn't like the mesh pocket in the front.
text_fidelity_b: bago Lightweight Small Hiking Backpack for Women and Men - 25L Travel Day Pack - Foldable Hiking Daypack Ultralight

text_fidelity_a:
Wenzel Evergreen Tent - 6 Person Update: We returned the original tent and dually had a chance to use the replacement sent and......

Same exact problem. Almost no wind, light rain and the poles bent at a ridiculous angle before snapping. Wenzel is the worst brand of tent I've ever used. Can't return it since it was last season's replacement so we sound up throwing what was left away. I regret not Judy buying a Coleman for the same price when I had the chance.
I'll start out saying that Wenzel in general is a very quality name and usually makes quality products. That being said I was very unhappy with this particular tent. Despite the usual common sense I have when I buy gear I didn't check the package before heading out (entirely my fault there). It's a good thing I keep a just in case kit in our vehicle because there were no pegs at all in the package, not even the little peg bag (and yes, It was bought new and still in the package as well as the Amazon box). No big deal there, just a minor annoyance.

I set the tent up with help of another avid camper friend of mine who's had this same exact tent for about a year and uses it like crazy. About two hours later a small sprinkling rain came up with some soft wind. His kids were enjoying tent time and listening to the rain when suddenly one of the poles splintered very quickly and sliced open my arm a few inches. suffice to say it was a very bad day and there were a several spooked and unhappy children as their dad had to take us all through the backwoods to a clinic so I could get stitches. Not the best birthday party a kid can have. I have had a couple of tents splinter their poles before but it's never been so violent nor had such a brittle quality to it. They've looked more like shreds while this just broke off in several jagged pieces and a few very sharp splinters left behind.

This is not the usual Wenzel quality and I'm hoping it's just a fluke. Perhaps it's the design? A badly handled or worn out pole? I don't know. But be aware that this might be a problem. Going through one of the many reviews I did find one where a woman had a pole splinter suddenly and go in to her hand. I wish I'd found that review before buying. I'm returning this one to Amazon for replacement in hopes that it was just one of those random things and will update if it happens again.
text_fidelity_b: Wenzel Evergreen Tent - 6 Person

text_fidelity_a: Foxelli Carbon Fiber Trekking Poles – Lightweight Collapsible Hiking Poles, Shock-Absorbent Walking Sticks with Natural Cork Grips, Flip Locks, 4 Season/All Terrain Accessories and Carry Bag First of all, I used to be one of those people who thought trekking poles were for wusses, but as I've gotten a bit older and wiser I have found that they are indispensable for longer hikes. I can hike twice as far with them and they really help with some challenging up and downs. These poles look great and are comfortable to use.  I went on one 10 mile hike when I first used them. I did find that the pole adjustment locks took some getting used to.  You have to turn a knob and then flip the clip to lock it into position. If you tighten the screw too much then there is too much tension and you can't flip the clip, so you have to go back and loosen the screw a bit more and then try again. Once I got the hang of it, it was fairly simple. I would suggest doing it before you leave the house. I'd also suggest leaning hard on each pole to be sure it's locked firmly.  Also, when putting the mud guards on, it helps to screw them on to the threads at the pole bases and then push on firmly. I lost one mudguard (in some really deep mud.) The Foxelli company's customer service is excellent though and they sent a replacement pair out right away!  These come with a nice bag and two sets of tips (one for storage and one for asphalt) and two sets of guards (one for dirt and one for snow.)
text_fidelity_b: Foxelli Carbon Fiber Trekking Poles – Lightweight Collapsible Hiking Poles, Shock-Absorbent Walking Sticks with Natural Cork Grips, Flip Locks, 4 Season/All Terrain Accessories and Carry Bag

TRX Training Essentials: Flexibility DVD, Workouts to Improve Flexibility I'm very impressed with suspension strap workouts. Doing strength training, instant adjustments to resistance are possible just by adjusting by an inch or two how close you are to the anchor. And almost every strength exercise, whether for arms or legs, also involves the core. Which is amazing.

But the best thing about the straps are for stretching and flexibility. I can get deeper, longer, more supported stretches with these then with any other method I've ever tried. And my friends have called me a stretch fanatic for years.

This DVD gives detailed descriptions of 10 or 12 stretches, with progressions for each one. Their "workout" is about 45 min. long. Or you can use the "exercise library" which gives detailed descriptions of each with their progressions. Watch the exercise library for a much shorter stretch workout or pause with your remote to work an individual stretch longer.

You can probably find most of these stretches on the internet, but I'm glad I got this DVD which I got in a 3 DVD package that included a strength and cardio DVD. The strength is a pretty good workout. Haven't tried the cardio yet.

Notice I haven't mentioned TRX once yet in this review. Although I do own a TRX and like it, you can get VERY similar suspension straps on Amazon for $24.99. I got RopeInaBag and use it for travel because it is much lighter and more compact while still being plenty strong.

Regardless of the brand of straps you use, I highly recommend the stretches in this DVD.
text_fidelity_b: TRX Training Essentials: Flexibility DVD, Workouts to Improve Flexibility

text_fidelity_a:
Kryptonite Keeper 785 Integrated Bicycle Lock Chain Bike Lock, 33.5-Inch, Red Bicycle locks come in lots of different strength/security levels. This is not a great lock. If you look at Kryptonite's web site, this is their cheapest and lightest weight chain lock. They give it a 5 out 10 rating. The Kryptonite Evolution chain lock gets an 8/10 rating and the Kryptonite New York chain gets a 10/10 rating. Those are both heavier and more expensive locks.

This Keeper lock is probably OK for lower risk situations, like daytime use at school or for short trips to the supermarket or a restaurant. It's also OK in rurals areas etc where there aren't a lot of bike thieves. This lock is much better than a cable lock (which mostly can be cut with small wire cutters), but a thief can probably still cut this with a heavy duty bolt cutter.

In the big city, this lock is far from sufficient as your only lock. Get a heavy duty lock as your primary lock (for your frame and rear wheel) and maybe use this as a secondary lock (for your front wheel).
text_fidelity_b: Kryptonite Keeper 785 Integrated Bicycle Lock Chain Bike Lock, 33.5-Inch, Red
